LESSON: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What do you consider when selecting materials from the library?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension
2. appreciate reading texts on peace building for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUE
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate reading texts on peace building for information

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate reading texts on peace building for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate reading texts on peace building for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate reading texts on peace building for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue to a partner. (skill: appreciate reading texts on peace building for information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate reading texts on peace building for information.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What do you consider when selecting materials from the library?
2. How can we ensure peace with others in the face of conflict?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create a list of vocabulary based on the theme for comprehension.
5. Be able to: appreciate reading texts on peace building for information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
